   Green Vernon Commission Agenda Report

Meeting Date:  December 17, 2025
From:  Genoveva Rocha, City Clerk
Department:  City Clerk
Submitted by:  Sandra Dolson, City Clerk Specialist

Subject
Selection of Chair and Vice Chair

Recommendation
Select one member to serve as Chairperson and one member to serve as Vice Chairperson for
the term ending on June 30, 2026.

Background
Pursuant to Vernon Municipal Code (VMC) Section 2.44.050(A), members are required to elect
a Chairperson and Vice Chairperson annually from different appointing categories under Section
2.44.020. Additionally, a member may not serve as Chairperson for more than two consecutive
annual terms. The VMC is silent on term limits for the Vice Chairperson.

The Green Vernon Commission consists of seven members, including three Vernon Business
Representatives, two labor Representatives, and two Representatives engaged in the
advancement of environmental and sustainability issues. Members serve four-year terms,
serving no more than two full consecutive terms.

Commissioner Browne was appointed as Chairperson on March 19, 2025. Commissioner Edry
was appointed to serve as Vice Chairperson on March 19, 2025. The current members are as
follows:

Commissioner  Appointing Category  Date Appointed End of Term
Jacquie Cabrera  Business Representative  August 5, 2025  June 30, 2026
Jack Cline  Business Representative  June 4, 2024  June 30, 2028
Ronit Edry  Business Representative  June 7, 2022  June 30, 2026
Catherine Browne  Environmental Representative June 7, 2022  June 30, 2026
Hector Morfin  Environmental Representative June 4, 2024  June 30, 2028
Martin Perez  Labor Representative  June 4, 2024  June 30, 2028
Stan Stosel  Labor Representative  June 4, 2024  June 30, 2028

All members of the Commission are eligible to serve as Chairperson and Vice Chairperson. The
Commission should select a Chairperson and Vice Chairperson to serve through June 30, 2026.

Fiscal Impact
There is no fiscal impact associated with this report.

Department:  Health and Environmental Control
Submitted by:  Dulce Gonzalez, Management Analyst

Subject
Helping Hands Edible Food Recovery Program Report

Recommendation
No action required by the Commission. This is a presentation only.

Background
Senate Bill (SB) 1383 mandates reducing organic waste disposal by implementing a fundamental
component to establish an edible food recovery program across all jurisdictions. This program
requires large food generators, including grocery stores, restaurants, and food service providers,
to donate surplus edible food to food recovery organizations rather than discarding it. The primary
objective is to redirect food that would otherwise be wasted to individuals in need. In alignment
with the City’s efforts to comply with SB 1383 requirements, the Health and Environmental
Control Department (Department) has formed a partnership with Helping Hands Society of Los
Angeles (Helping Hands) to facilitate the recovery of eligible food items and accept donations
from local businesses.

Helping Hands is a 501(c)(3) non-profit organization supporting the City’s food recovery efforts.
Helping Hands supplies perishable and non-perishable food items, personal hygiene products,
and clothing to small food pantries, charitable organizations, distribution centers, and other non-
profits. Since commencing operations in 2021, Helping Hands has emerged as a vital asset to
the community. It has engaged in numerous City events and is cultivating strong relationships
with local businesses to enhance donation levels and address food insecurity.

The collaboration between the City and this non-profit leverages Helping Hands' existing
infrastructure and community relationships to create a seamless and efficient food recovery
program. The Department is working with Helping Hands to:

  •  Identify and Connect Food Generators: The Department identifies large food generators
  within Vernon and connects them to Helping Hands to establish regular donation routes.
  •  Track Compliance: The partnership includes a system for monitoring the volume of
  donated food to ensure compliance with mandated edible food recovery targets.
  •  Promote Community Engagement: The Department and Helping Hands jointly promote
  the program to encourage more local businesses to participate.

This partnership is essential for achieving SB 1383 compliance and broader community
objectives. Representatives from Helping Hands will provide a presentation to the Commission
on their initiatives and progress.

Fiscal Impact
There is no fiscal impact associated with this report.

March 19, 2025

PRESENTATIONS

1.  Selection of Chair and Vice Chair
  Recommendation:
  Select one member to serve as Chair and one member to serve as Vice Chair for
  the term ending June 30, 2025.

  Deputy City Clerk Parker presented the staff report.

MOTION
  Commissioner Perez moved for Commissioner Edry to serve as chair. The motion
  received no second.

  Clarification was provided to the Commission that the municipal code outlines the
  position of Chair as a one-year term and has a two consecutive term limit. Chair
  Edry had served in the position of Chair for two consecutive terms and met the
  threshold for terming out for the Chairperson position.

  Commissioner Browne added she would be willing to serve as Chair for two
  months and re-select Chair Edry the next cycle for another one-year term, which
  would comply with the Code.

  Commissioner Browne moved and Chair Edry seconded a motion to select
  Commissioner Browne to serve as Chair for the term ending June 30, 2025. The
  question was called and the motion carried 5-0, Vice Chair Gazcon and
  Commissioner Morfin absent.

MOTION
  Commissioner Cline moved and Commissioner Browne seconded a motion to
  select Commissioner Edry to serve as Vice Chair for the term ending June 30,
  2025. The question was called and the motion carried 5-0, Commissioners Gazcon
  and Morfin absent.

  Chairperson Browne moved and received consensus from the Commission for
  Vice Chair Edry to continue to chair the meeting.

2.  Vernon’s Public EV Charging Infrastructure Update
  Recommendation:
  No action required by the Commission. This is an update presentation only.

  Public Utilities Assistant General Manager Otto presented the staff report and
  Customer Relations and Marketing Manager Sun presented the accompanying
  PowerPoint.
